file.content: Todos

lines: +  // [REQ-009] Complete every todo. The array is not reordered, so insertion order still breaks priority ties.
+  // [REQ-009] Remove every completed todo; active todos keep their order.
// [REQ-005] Highest priority first; insertion order within the same priority. Does not mutate items.

content.text:
I added two buttons below the list. "Mark all complete" (`bulk-mark-all`) completes every todo, and "Clear completed" (`bulk-clear-completed`) deletes the completed ones. Both change the saved list directly, and the existing sort still sets the order: completed todos below active ones, high to low priority, and the order you added them within the same priority. I haven't run or tested it in a browser.
Both act on every todo, even ones hidden by the current search or filter. Clicking "Mark all complete" again does nothing, because it never un-completes a todo.
I didn't limit the actions to visible todos, and I didn't make "Mark all" a toggle.
